definitions.explanation: Used to draw a comparison, typically followed by ようだ/みたいだ.
Used with negative expressions to mean 'not at all'.

examples.japanese: まるで{夢|ゆめ}のようだった。
examples.english: It was just like a dream.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はまるで{子供|こども}みたいに{泣|な}いた。
examples.english: He cried just like a child.

notes:
USAGE PATTERNS:

1. まるで〜ようだ/みたいだ (just like ~)
・まるで{夢|ゆめ}のようだ (just like a dream)
・まるで{嘘|うそ}みたいだ (it's like a lie - unbelievable)

2. まるで〜ない (not at all, completely not)
・まるで{分|わ}からない (don't understand at all)
・まるで{違|ちが}う (completely different)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・まるで - emphasizes strong resemblance or total negation
・ちょうど - exactly like
・あたかも - as if (more literary)
